outcomes: A workload that spans the Go and TypeScript runtimes points both at one OTLP/HTTP collector
A dashboard finds the HTTP server metrics of a Go and a TypeScript service under the same names, units, labels and buckets
Telemetry never fails or stalls the workload that produces it
The CLI and the usage receiver enforce one closed vocabulary, so a usage record carries no free text
A server span parents to the client span that called it, even when a proxy between them rewrites the parent ID of traceparent
nonGoals: A /metrics scrape endpoint, gRPC OTLP, statsd or a Prometheus push gateway: OTLP/JSON over HTTP is the one transport, as ADR 0001 records
An OpenTelemetry exporter SDK dependency: the envelope is written against the wire format
Whether the CLI sends usage telemetry, and its notice and opt-out, which the CLI owns

requirements.text: ProtocolVersion is 1, and a test pins it, so a changed field name or encoding, a new required field or a changed canonical serialization is a reviewed version bump.

text: The signals are metrics, traces and logs, posted as application/json to /v1/metrics, /v1/traces and /v1/logs on the collector base URL.
An unknown signal has no path.
The Go log sink posts its records to /v1/logs as a logs request that validates.

requirements.text: The canonical resource attribute keys are service.name, service.version, putnami.framework and service.instance.id, in that order. service.name is required; a runtime populates the others when it knows them, and service.instance.id names the process that pushes.

text: The contract pins an exporter's defaults: logs flush every 10 s, metrics every 60 s, and spans leave in batches of at most 512 at most 30 s apart; a request times out after 5 s, shutdown flushes once more, a failed batch is dropped, and the queue holds at most 10000 records.
Both runtimes test their export defaults against fixtures/conventions/export-contract.json.
The Go metric reader flushes once more on shutdown, and the Go exporter swallows a collector error rather than return it.
Each signal request parses strictly, and an unknown member is refused.
Every valid fixture of the three signals parses clean and every invalid one is refused, and every reject branch of a metrics data point has an invalid fixture of its own.

requirements.text: The protocol registers exactly 13 telemetry.* codes: an invalid metrics, traces or logs request, and an invalid metric, data point, attribute, resource, span, trace ID, span ID, temporality, log record or severity.

text: MarshalCanonical turns the fixed input of each signal into exactly the bytes of its committed golden, and those bytes hash to a pinned SHA-256 digest.
The TypeScript renderer of @putnami/application builds the same input and reproduces the three digests.
A log level maps to its OTLP severity number: trace, debug, info, warn or warning, error and fatal.
An unknown or uppercase level maps to 0, unspecified.
BoolVal and DoubleVal set exactly one value kind.
The Go runtime maps its metric temporality, span status and log levels to the OTLP numbers.
Every runtime records each HTTP request it serves as http.server.request_count, a counter, and http.server.duration, a histogram in ms, both labeled http.method, http.route and http.status_code.
http.route is the route pattern, never the request path.
Both runtimes test against fixtures/conventions/http-server-metrics.json.

Every runtime keeps a root span while the instance has kept fewer than telemetry.traces.budget roots, or while the current UTC minute holds fewer than telemetry.traces.floorPerMinute kept roots, or when telemetry.traces.ratio picks its trace ID, and drops it otherwise.
The ratio picks a trace ID whose last 8 bytes, read big-endian and shifted right one bit, are below the ratio times 2^63.
Both runtimes test against fixtures/conventions/trace-sampling.json.
The defaults are a budget of 100 roots, a ratio of 0.01 and a floor of 1 root per minute; a budget and a floor are whole numbers of 0 or more, and a ratio lies between 0 and 1.
A span with a parent, remote or local, follows the parent's sampled flag and makes no decision.
Each root decision counts once in the counter trace.decisions, labeled outcome kept or dropped.
Without a valid traceparent a server has no remote parent.
When x-putnami-traceparent is a valid version 00 value with the trace ID of traceparent and another parent ID, the server span parents to it, flags included.
Otherwise the server uses traceparent.
Both runtimes test against fixtures/conventions/proxy-safe-traceparent.json.

A client that injects its span context into an outgoing call writes the same version 00 value to traceparent and to x-putnami-traceparent, so a proxy that rewrites traceparent leaves the client's span in the second header.
cliusage pins the closed vocabulary of CLI usage records: the event names, the attributes each event allows and requires with their value kinds, the error categories and the command names.
A conforming record validates, a record outside the vocabulary is refused, a request from another service is refused, and every required attribute is also allowed.

requirements.text: A command name that a released CLI sends never leaves the vocabulary, and every name is a unique lowercase token of at most 64 characters that starts with a letter, so the receiver keeps the records of every released CLI and its aggregate keys stay bounded.

text: cliusage/otlp-logs.golden.json is a valid logs request that conforms to the vocabulary.
The CLI encodes a session into exactly those bytes and refuses to record an event outside the vocabulary.
The receiver keeps a conforming record and rewrites its integers in canonical decimal form.
Every runtime counts each log record as log.records, a counter labeled level, one of debug, info, warn and error, and outcome, emitted or dropped.
Both runtimes test against fixtures/conventions/log-records.json.
